text_en: Most of the items buried with Tutankhamun have been well preserved, including thousands of artefacts made from precious metals and rare stones.

text: Kũgundũra kwa magũrũ merũ mena Cuma kana mbaũ gatagatĩ gwatũmire chariots cia Assyrians ihũthe, itengere na ikorwo ciĩharĩirie wega gũcinda chariots icio ingĩ.
text_en: The invention of spoke wheels made Assyrian chariots lighter, faster, and better prepared to outrun soldiers and other chariots.

text: Matimũ ma kuma ũta ũcio wao mũũru no matũrĩkanĩrie ngo-inĩ cia mbũtũ thũ ciao. Kindu B.C ngiri ĩmwe, Assyrians makĩrehe mbũtũ ya mbere ĩrĩa yarũagĩra barathi-inĩ kana ngaari ciĩna matharaita.
text_en: Arrows from their deadly crossbows could penetrate the armor of rival soldiers. About 1000 B.C., the Assyrians introduced the first cavalry.

text: Calvary nĩ mbũtũ iria irũagĩra ikuĩtwo mũgongo-inĩ wa mbarathi. Gĩtĩ gĩa gũikarĩra mbarathĩ hĩndĩ ĩyo gĩtiahumbũrĩtwo, kwa ũguo mbũtũ icio cia mbarathi cia Assyria ciarũaga ciikarĩire mĩgongo ĩyo ya mbarathi irĩ utheri.
text_en: A cavalry is an army that fights on horseback. The saddle had not yet been invented, so the Assyrian cavalry fought on the bare backs of their horses.

text: Nĩ tũĩ ateti aingĩ a Greece, scientists na atungi maũndũ na aini. Makĩria, mũndũ ũrĩa ũĩkaine mũno wa ũndũire ũcio nĩ Homer, ũrĩa wa menyekanĩte mũno hau gatene eta gĩtumumu na mugi marebeta, ũrĩa watungire mawĩra ma ũtungi merĩ wandĩki-inĩ wa mabuku Greece: marebeta ta Iliad na Odissey
text_en: We know many Greek politicians, scientists, and artists. Possibly the most known person of this culture is Homer, the legendary blind poet, who composed two masterpieces of Greek literature: the poems Iliad and Odyssey.

text: Sophocles na Aristophanes nĩ mathako moĩkaine mũno, na mũthakĩre wamo nĩ wonekaga ũrĩ ũmwe wa wĩra ũrĩa mwega mũno wandĩki-inĩ wa mabuku.
text_en: Sophocles and Aristophanes are still popular playwrights and their plays are considered to be among the greatest works of world literature.

text: Mũndũ ũngĩ ũĩkaine mũno wa Greece nĩ mwĩki mathabu wĩtagwo Pythagoras, ũrĩa ũĩkaine mũno nĩ ũndũ wa thiorĩ yake ya ũrĩa mĩena ĩtatũ ya right triangles ĩtainio.
text_en: Another famous Greek is a mathematician Pythagoras, mostly known for his famous theorem about relations of the sides of right triangles.

text: Kwĩna matanya maingĩ ma namba ya andũ arĩa maragia kĩhĩndĩ. Nĩ kwĩrĩkanaga atĩ nĩruo rũthiomi rũrĩa rwaragio mũno gatagatĩ ka namba igĩrĩ nginya inya thĩ yothe.
text_en: There are varying estimates for how many people speak Hindi. It is estimated to be between the second and fourth most commonly spoken language in the world.

text: Namba ya aikari arĩa kĩhumo kĩao nĩ kũu ĩkoragwo na ũtiganũ kũringana na kana thiomi iria ikuhanĩrĩirie mũno nĩ iratarwo.
text_en: The number of native speakers varies depending on whether or not very closely related dialects are counted.

text: Arĩa meciragĩrio gũkorwo marĩ gatagatĩ ka million magana matatũ ma mĩrongo ĩna nginya million magana matano, na angĩ matanyihĩirie million magana manana no mataũkĩrwo nĩ rũthiomi rũu.
text_en: Estimates range from 340 million to 500 million speakers, and as many as 800 million people can understand the language.

text: Hĩndĩ na Urdu nĩ ihanaine harĩ marĩtwa maritũ no ũtigithũkanu harĩ mĩandĩkĩre; mĩario-inĩ ya o mũthenya, na arĩa a thiomi cierĩ no maiguithanie.
text_en: Hindi and Urdu are similar in vocabulary but different in script; in everyday conversations, speakers of both languages can usually understand each other.

text: Kĩndũ century ya ikũmi na gatano, Estonia ya mwena wa rũgongo yarĩ rungu rwa mogucĩriria ma ũndũire wa Germany.
text_en: Around the 15th century, northern Estonia was under great cultural influence of Germany.

text: Atungatĩri a monks kuma Germany nĩ mendaga kurehe Ngai hakuhĩ na andũ a kũu, ko ũguo magĩthondeka rũthiomi rwa kĩ Estonia.
text_en: Some German monks wanted to bring God closer to the native people, so they invented the Estonian literal language.

text: Rwathondeketwo kũringana na mũrũmanĩrĩrio wa ndemwa cia Jerumani na ndemwa ĩmwe "Õ/õ" nĩyongereirwo.
text_en: It was based on the German alphabet and one character "Õ/õ" was added.

text: O ũrĩa kahinda gathiaga, marĩtwa maingĩ makũhoya kuma kũrĩ Germany makĩnyitana. Gĩkĩ nĩkĩo kĩarĩ kĩambĩrĩria kĩa ũũgĩ.
text_en: As time passed, many words that were borrowed from German coalesced. This was the beginning of enlightenment.

text: kũringana na ũndũire, mũgai wa wathani agĩrĩirwo nĩ kũingĩra mbũtũ-inĩ o rio thutha wa kũrĩkia cukuru.
text_en: Traditionally, the heir to the throne would go straight into the military after finishing school.

text: Ona kũrĩ ũguo, Charles athiire cukuru mũnene kũu Cambridge, kũrĩa athomeire Anthropology na Archeology na thutha History na akĩgia 2:2 (lower second class degree).
text_en: However, Charles went to university at Trinity College, Cambridge where he studied Anthropology and Archaeology, and later History, earning a 2:2 (a lower second class degree).

text: Charles arĩ mũmemba wa mbere wa British Royal Family kuheo kĩheo kĩa degree.
text_en: Charles was the first member of the British Royal Family to be awarded a degree.

text: European Turkey (mwena wa irathĩro rĩa Thrace kana Rumeliathĩiniĩ wa Balkan peninsula) ĩkoragwo na mũigana wa 3% wa bũrũri ũyũ.
text_en: European Turkey (eastern Thrace or Rumelia in the Balkan peninsula) includes 3% of the country.

text: Turkey ĩkoragwo na ũraihu wa kiromita 1,600 (mairũ 1,000) na wariĩ wa kiromita 800 (mairũ 500) na ĩkoragwo na mũhiano wa rectangle.
text_en: The territory of Turkey is more than 1,600 kilometres (1,000 mi) long and 800 km (500 mi) wide, with a roughly rectangular shape.

text: Mũigana wa Turkey hamwe na maria, ũkoragwo 783,563 square kilometers (300,948 sq mi) kũrĩa 755,688 ĩkoragwo south west Asia na 23,764 square kilometers (9,174 sq mi) ciĩ Europe.
text_en: Turkey's area, including lakes, occupies 783,562 square kilometres (300,948 sq mi), of which 755,688 square kilometres (291,773 sq mi) are in south west Asia and 23,764 square kilometres (9,174 sq mi) in Europe.

text: Mũigana wa Turkey ũtũmĩte ĩkorwo bũrũri wa 37 kũrĩ ũnene thĩiniĩ wa thĩ, na nĩ ta mũigana wa Metropolitan France na United Kingdom ciĩ hamwe.
text_en: Turkey's area makes it the world's 37th-largest country, and is about the size of Metropolitan France and the United Kingdom combined.

text: Turkey ĩrigicĩirio nĩ irĩma mĩena ĩtatũ: Aegean Sea mwena wa ithũĩro, Black Sea mwena wa rũgũrũ na Mediterranean Sea mwena wa mũhuro.
text_en: Turkey is encircled by seas on three sides: the Aegean Sea to the west, the Black Sea to the north and the Mediterranean Sea to the south.

text: Luxembourg ĩkoragwo na historĩ ndaihu no wĩyathi wayo wambĩrĩirie 1839.
text_en: Luxembourg has a long history but its independence dates from 1839.

text: Icigo imwe cia Belgium ciakoragwo irĩ icigo cia Luxembourg hĩndi ya tene no igĩtuika cia Belgium thuutha wa Belgian Revolution.
text_en: Present-day parts of Belgium were part of Luxembourg in the past but became Belgian after the 1830s Belgian Revolution.

text: Luxembourg ĩkoretwo ĩkĩgeria gũkorwo ĩtekũnyita mbaru mwena o wothe no nĩyetahĩirwo nĩ Geremani hĩndĩ ya World War I na World war II.
text_en: Luxembourg has always tried to remain a neutral country but it was occupied in both World War I and World War II by Germany.

text: Kũrĩ 1957, Luxembourg nĩyatuĩkire memba wa kwambĩrĩria kĩũngano kĩrĩa kĩũĩkaine ũmũthĩ ta European Union.
text_en: In 1957 Luxembourg became a founding member of the organization which is today known as the European Union.

text: Drukryal Dzong nĩ fortress na gĩikaro kĩa Buddhist gĩthũku kĩrĩa gĩkoragwo rũgongo rwa Paro District (thĩiniĩ wa Phondey Village).
text_en: The Drukgyal Dzong is a ruined fortress and Buddhist monastery in the upper part of the Paro District (in Phondey Village).

text: Kwĩrĩkanaga atĩ kũrĩ 1649, Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyel nĩwe wathondekete fortless ĩno gũkũngũĩra ũhotani wake kũrĩ mbutũ ya Tibetan-Mongol.
text_en: It is said that in 1649, Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyel created the fortress to commemorate his victory against the Tibetan-Mongol forces.

text: kũrĩ 1951, mwaki niwatũmire icunjĩ imwe cia Drukgyal Dzong itigare ta mbica ya Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyel.
text_en: In 1951, a fire caused for only some of the relics of the Drukgyal Dzong to remain, such as the image of Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal.

text: Thuutha wa mwaki, fortless nĩyahingirwo na ĩkĩmenyererwo nginya ĩgĩtuika kĩrorerwo kĩnene thĩiniĩ wa Bhutan.
text_en: After the fire, the fortress was preserved and protected, remaining to be one of Bhutan's most sensational attractions.

text: Kũrĩ century ya 18, Cambodia yekorire ĩhinyĩrĩirio nĩ mabũrũri meerĩ mena hinya, Thailand na Vietnam.
text_en: During the 18th century Cambodia found itself squeezed between two powerful neighbors, Thailand and Vietnam.

text: Kũrĩ century ya 18, andũ a Thailand nĩmatharĩkĩire Cambodia maita maigana ũna na kũrĩ 1772, nĩmathũkangirie Phnom Phen.
text_en: The Thais invaded Cambodia several times in the 18th century and in 1772 they destroyed Phnom Phen.

text: Mĩaka-inĩ ya mũthia ya century ya 18 andũ a Vietnam onao nĩmatharĩkĩire Cambodia.
text_en: In the last years of the 18th century the Vietnamese also invaded Cambodia.

text: Gĩcunjĩ kĩa ikũmi na inyanya harĩ igana kĩa andũ a Venezuela matikoragwo mandĩkĩtwo wĩra, na aingĩ a arĩa aandĩke marutaga wĩra ũtarĩ wa wabici.
text_en: Eighteen percent of Venezuelans are unemployed, and most of those who are employed work in the informal economy.

text: Andũ eerĩ harĩ atatũ a Venezuela arĩa marutaga wĩra marutaga thĩiniĩ wa ũtungata, hakuhĩ robo marutaga iganda-inĩ and ũmwe harĩ atano nĩ arĩmi.
text_en: Two thirds of Venezuelans who work do so in the service sector, nearly a quarter work in industry and a fifth work in agriculture.

text: Kĩganda kĩrĩa gĩa bata mũno thĩiniĩ wa Venezuela nĩ maguta, kũrĩa bũrũri ũyũ wendagia maguta na nja, ona o korwo nĩ gĩcunjĩ kĩa imwe harĩ igana marutaga wĩra iganda-inĩ cia maguta.
text_en: An important industry for Venezuelans is oil, where the country is a net exporter, even though only one percent work in the oil industry.

text: Kĩambĩrĩrĩ-inĩ kĩa wĩyathi wa bũrũri, ataaramu a Botanic Gardens a Singapore nĩmateithĩrĩirie kũgarũra gĩcigĩrĩra gĩkĩ kĩa iria-inĩ nginyagia gĩgĩtuĩka taũni ĩna mĩmera mĩingĩ.
text_en: Early in the nation's independence, Singapore Botanic Gardens' expertise helped to transform the island into a tropical Garden City.

text: Kũrĩ 1981, Vanda Miss Joaquim, orchid ya gũciarithanio, nĩrĩathurirwo tarĩ rĩo ihũa rĩa gĩbũrũri.
text_en: In 1981, Vanda Miss Joaquim, an orchid hybrid, was chosen as the nation's national flower.

text: O mwaka mweri-inĩ wa Oktoba, nyamũ iria irĩaga mĩmera hakuhĩ mirioni 1.5 nĩithiaga mwena wa nyanjara-inĩ cia mũhuro, cikaringa rũũĩ rwa Mara kuuma irĩma-inĩ cia mwena wa rũgũrũ cikĩrũmĩrĩra mbura.
text_en: Every year around October nearly 1.5 million herbivores travel towards the southern plains, crossing the Mara River, from the northern hills for the rains.

text: Cigacoka rĩngĩ mwena wa rũgũrũ kũhĩtũkĩra ithũĩro, o rĩngĩ cigakĩra rũũĩ rwa Mara thuutha wa mbura gũthira mweri-inĩ wa April.
text_en: And then back to the north through the west, once again crossing the Mara river, after the rains in around April.

text: Serengeti ĩkoragwo na Serengeti National Park, Ngorongoro Conservation Area na Maswa Game Reserve thĩinĩi wa Tanzania na Maasai Mara National Reserve thĩinĩi wa Kenya.
text_en: The Serengeti region contains the Serengeti National Park, the Ngorongoro Conservation Area and Maswa Game Reserve in Tanzania and the Maasai Mara National Reserve in Kenya.

text: Kwĩruta gũthondeka interactive media kwendaga ũjuzi wa kĩĩrĩu na gĩtene hamwe na indo iria irũtanĩtwo irathi-inĩ cia interactive (kwandĩka rũgano, mũgambo, video, editing, kũgana, na ingĩ).
text_en: Learning to create interactive media requires conventional and traditional skills, as well as tools mastered in interactive classes (storyboarding, audio and video editing, story telling, etc.)

text: Interactive design yendaga wĩrore ũrĩa wĩtĩkĩtie ũndũ wĩgiĩ media na wĩrute kwaga gwĩciria na njĩra ĩmwe.
text_en: Interactive design requires that you re-assess your assumptions about media production and learn to think in a non-linear ways.

text: 1300- Interactive design yendaga atĨ tũindo tuothe twa projectĨ nitũratwarana na bado nĨtwĨrũgamirĨire tũrĨ twiki.
text_en: Interactive design requires that components of a project connect to each other, but also make sense as a separate entity.

text: Hari ũndũ ũrĨa mũũru ukonainiĨ na icicio cia zoom nĨ atĨ mũigana na ũritu wa icicio urĨa wendekaga nigetha kũgĨa na mbica njega nĨ munene mũno gũkĨra wa icicio cia prime.
text_en: The disadvantage of zoom lenses is that the focal complexity and number of lens elements required to achieve a range of focal lengths is much greater than for prime lenses.

text: KĨũndũ gĨki nĨkĨratiga gũtuĨka thĨna tondũ athondeki a icicio ici nĨmahotete gũthondeka icicio ciĨna ikĨro cia igũrũ.
text_en: This is becoming less of an issue as lens manufacturers achieve higher standards in lens production.

text: KĨũndũ gĨkĨ kĨhotithĨtie kũrutwo kwa mbica njega ikĨringithanio na iria cia gacicio karĨa gatagucagia mbica.
text_en: This has allowed zoom lenses to produce pictures of a quality comparable to that achieved by lenses with fixed focal length.

text: KĨũndũ kĨngĨ kĨũru gĨkonainie na icicio cia zoom nĨ atĨ aperture irĨa ya igũrũ (ihenya) rĨa gicicio nĨ atĨ nĨ inini.
text_en: Another disadvantage of zoom lenses is that the maximum aperture (the speed) of the lens is usually lower.

text: GĨtũmi gĨkĨ gĨtũmaga icicio cia zoom iria itarĨ goro ikoro na hinya kũhũthika kũndũ gutarĨ na ũtheri mũingĨ hatarĨ na utheri wayo.
text_en: This makes inexpensive zoom lenses hard to use in low-light conditions without a flash.

text: Thĩna ũrĩa mũnene hĩndi ya kũgeria gũcenjia thenema  ĩtuĩke DVD nĩ overscan.
text_en: One of the most common problems when trying to convert a movie to DVD format is the overscan.

text: TV nyingĩ cithondeketwo nĩguo cikenie mũingĩ.
text_en: Most televisions are made in a way to please the general public.

text: Gwa gĩtũmi kĩu, kĩndũ kĩrĩa gĩothe wonaga TV inĩ kĩarĩ na mĩhaka ĩtinitio igũrũ, thĩ na mĩena.
text_en: For that reason, everything you see on the TV had the borders cut, top, bottom and sides.

text: ũndũ ũyũ wĩkagwo nĩguo mbica iihũre gĩcicioinĩ gĩothe. ũndu ũyũ witagwo overscan.
text_en: This is made to ensure that the image covers the whole screen. That is called overscan.

text: Kwa mutino, ungĩthondeka DVD, kwĩna uhoteku ĩtinio mĩicoinĩ, na angĩkorwo thenema nĩ irarĩ na tũcunjĩ tũkuhĩrĩirie thi, tutikuonanio tuothe.
text_en: Unfortunately, when you make a DVD, it's borders will most likely be cut too, and if the video had subtitles too close to the bottom, they won't be fully shown.

text: Mĩako ya tene ya nyũmba cia athamaki nĩikoretwo ĩcũngĩrĩirie meciria na kũrehe mbica cia haro mecirianĩ na cia mbarathi cia Arthur.
text_en: The traditional medieval castle has long inspired the imagination, conjuring up images of jousts, banquets and Arthurian chivalry.

text: Ona ĩrũgamĩtio gatagatĩ ka matigari ma mĩako ya mĩaka ngiri ĩmwe nĩ ũhũthũ kũririkana mĩgambo na mĩnungo ya mbara thiru, hakuhĩ kũigua makinya ma mbarathi igũrũ rĩa mĩaro ya mahiga na kũigua mũnungo wa guoya ũkiuma marima ma kũiga ohũo.
text_en: Even standing amidst thousand year-old ruins it is easy to bring to mind the sounds and smells of battles long gone, to almost hear the clatter of hooves on the cobbles and to smell the fear rising from the dungeon pits.

text: No mwĩcirĩrie witũ nĩũrugamĩtio na ma? Nyũmba nene cia athamaki ciakagwo nĩkĩ? Ciacorirwo na cigĩakwo atĩa?
text_en: But is our imagination based on reality? Why were castles built in the first place? How were they designed and built?

text: O ta ũrĨa kwaarĨ hĨndĨ Ĩyo, Kirby Muxloe Castle yaarĨ nyũmba ngitĨre mũno gũkĨra castle iria ingĨ.
text_en: Typical for the period, Kirby Muxloe Castle is more of a fortified house than a true castle.

text: Ndirica ciayo iria ciarĨ na icicio nene na thingo ciayo njeke citingĨahotire gwĨtirĨrĨa tharĨkĨra nene gwa kahinda karaihu.
text_en: Its large glazed windows and thin walls would not have been able to resist a determined attack for long.

text: KũrĨ mĨaka-inĨ ya 1840s, rĨrĨa waaki wayo wambĨrĨirio nĨ Lord Hastings, bũrũri waarĨ na thaayu mũno na ũgitĨri wendekaga harĨ tũkundi tũnini twa mĨkora.
text_en: In the 1480s, when its construction was begun by Lord Hastings, the country was relatively peaceful and defense was only required against small bands of roving marauders.

text: WĨiganania wa maahinya waarĨ mũbango wa thĨ cia rũraya harĨa ciendaga kũmenyerera wĨyathi wa gĨbũrũri wa mabũrũri moothe ma rũraya.
text_en: The balance of power was a system in which European nations sought to maintain the national sovereignty of all European states.

text: Mũbango ũyũ waarĨ atĨ mabũrũri moothe ma rũraya maarĨ marigĨrĨrie bũrũri ũmwe gũkorwo na hinya, na nĨũndũ ũcio thirikari cia mabũrũri nĨciacenjagia athiriti nĨũndũ wa kũiganania maahinya.
text_en: The concept was that all European nations had to seek to prevent one nation from becoming powerful, and thus national governments often changed their alliances in order to maintain the balance.

text: Mbaara ya Spanish nĨyo yaarĨ mbaara ya mbere ĨrĨa yaumanire na kũgeria kũiganania maahinya.
text_en: The War of Spanish Succession marked the first war whose central issue was the balance of power.

text: KwagĨire na ũgarũrũku mũnene tondũ mabũrũri maria maarĨ hinya rũraya matingĨambĨrĨirie mbaara makiuga atĨ nĨ cia kĨndini. Kwoguo mbaara ino ya mĨaka mĨrongo Ĩtatu yaarĨ ya mũico gwĨto mbaara ya kĨndini.
text_en: This marked an important change, as European powers would no longer have the pretext of being religious wars. Thus, the Thirty Years' War would be the last war to be labeled a religious war.

text: Mũthigiti wa Artemis kũrĩa Ephesus wathũkirio kũrĩ Julai 21, 356 BCE kuhĩtũkĩra gũcinwo nĩ Herostratus.
text_en: The temple of Artemis at Ephesus was destroyed on July 21, 356 BCE in an act of arson committed by Herostratus.

text: Kũringana na rũgano, arongoreirie kũgĩa ngumo kwa njĩra o yoothe. Aebeso, nĩũndũ wa kũrakara, makiuga atĩ rĩtwa Herostranus rĩtikanandĩkwo.
text_en: According to the story, his motivation was fame at any cost. The Ephesians, outraged, announced that Herostratus' name never be recorded.

text: Strabo, ũrĩa waarĩ historian wa Greek, thuutha nĩandĩkire rĩtwa rĩake, na ũũ nĩguo twarĩmenyire. Mũthigiti wathũkirio ũtukũ ũrĩa Alexander the Great aciarirwo.
text_en: The Greek historian Strabo later noted the name, which is how we know today. The temple was destroyed on the same night that Alexander the Great was born.

text: Alexander, arĩ mũthamaki, nĩerutĩire gwaka mũthigiti rĩngĩ, no wendi wake ũkĩregwo. Thuutha wa Alexander gũkua, muthigiti nĩwakirwo rĩngĩ kũrĩ 323 BCE.
text_en: Alexander, as king, offered to pay to rebuild the temple, but his offer was denied. Later, after Alexander died, the temple was rebuilt in 323 BCE.

text: TĨtĨrithia atĨ guoko gũaku gũtirĨ na mĨhĨnga ta ũrĨa kwahoteka o ũgĨthiaga na mbere kũhihinya batoni ciothe o ũrĨa kwagiriire- geria nduũgaikie twara twaku mũno.
text_en: Make sure your hand is as relaxed as possible while still hitting all the notes correctly - also try not to make much extraneous motion with your fingers.

text: Kwa njĨra Ĩno, ndũkũnoga mũno. Ririkana atĨ hatirĨ bata wa kũgũtha keys na hinya atĨ niguo irute mũgambo mũnene ta piano.
text_en: This way, you will tire yourself out as little as possible. Remember there's no need to hit the keys with a lot of force for extra volume like on the piano.

text: Accordion nayo, nĨgetha ũgĨe mũgambo mũnene, ũhũthagĨra bellows na pressure kana ihenya inene.
text_en: On the accordion, to get extra volume, you use the bellows with more pressure or speed.

text: Mysticism nĨ kũrũmĨrĨra gĨathĨ na, kwĨiguithania na, kana kũmenya na ngoro ũma wa Ngai na roho.
text_en: Mysticism is the pursuit of communion with, identity with, or conscious awareness of an ultimate reality, divinity, spiritual truth, or God.

text: MwĨtĨkia acaragia kwĨiguithania Ĩmwe kwa Ĩmwe na kũmenyana na ngai mũũmbi.
text_en: The believer seeks a direct experience, intuition, or insight into divine reality/the deity or dieties.

text: EtĨkia marũmagĨrĨra njĨra njega cia mũikarĨre irĨa cimateithagĨrĨria gũkinyanĨria wĨtĨkio wao.
text_en: Followers pursue certain ways of living, or practices that are intended to nurture those experiences.

text: Mysticism no Ĩtigithũkanio kuuma kũrĨ mĨthemba ĨngĨ ya wĨtĨkio na kũgooca nĨ gũkorwo ĨtĨtĨrithagia ũhoro wĨigainie na ũmũndũ mũnomũno marĨa megainie na thayũ, gĨkeno, na kuihurĨrĨrwo.
text_en: Mysticism can be distinguished from other forms of religious belief and worship by its emphasis on the direct personal experience of a unique state of consciousness, particularly those of a peaceful, insightful, blissful, or even ecstatic character.

text: Sikhism nĨ gĨthoomo kũũma gĨcigĨrĨra-inĨ kĨa India. Yaumire mwena wa Punjab kũrĨ century ya 15 kũma kwĨ mwahũ wa sectarian ũrĨa wĨ ũndũire-inĨ wa Hindu.
text_en: Sikhism is a religion from the Indian sub-continent. It originated in the Punjab region during the 15th century from a sectarian split within the Hindu tradition.

text: Sikhs monaga wĨtĨkio wao ta ndini ngũrani na Hinduism ona akorwo nĨmetĨkĨraga atĨ yumanĨte na ũndũire wa Hindu.
text_en: Sikhs consider their faith to be a separate religion from Hinduism though they acknowledge its Hindu roots and traditions.

text: Sikhs metaga ndini yao Gurmat, irĨa yumanĨte na Punjabi kuuga "njĨra ya guru." Guru nĨ muthingi wa bata harĨ ndini ciothe cia India no harĨ Sikhism nĨĨrĨ bata makĨria na nĨyo kĨhumo kĨa wĨtĨkio wa Sikh.
text_en: Sikhs call their religion Gurmat, which is Punjabi for "way of the guru". The guru is a fundamental aspect of all Indian religions but in Sikhism has taken on an importance that forms the core of Sikh beliefs.

text: Ndini Ĩno yambĨrĨirio century ya 15 nĨ Guru Nanak (1469-1539). Thutha ucio nĨkwagĨire na gurus angĨ kenda.
text_en: The religion was founded in the 15th century by Guru Nanak (1469–1539). There followed in succession a further nine gurus.

text: Ona kũrĨ o ũguo, kurĨ Juni 1956, ciĨraniro cia Krushchev nĨciageririo hĨndĨ ya mĨrũrũngano poland, kũrĨa aruti a wĨra mareganaga na ũnyihu wa irio na gũtinio mĨcara, yagarũrũkire na ĨgĨtũĨka uregani harĨ communism.
text_en: However, in June 1956, Krushchev's promises were put to the test when riots in Poland, where workers were protesting against food shortages and wage cuts, turned into a general protest against Communism.

text: Ona gũtuĨka muico-inĨ, Krushchev nĨatũmire ibaaru gũcokia thaayũ, nĨetĨkĨrire maũndũ mamwe na agĨtĨkĨra gũthuura Wladyslaw Gomulka ũrĨa waarĨ ngumo gũtuĨka mĨnĨsta mũkaru.
text_en: Although in the end, Krushchev sent in tanks to restore order, he did give way to some economic demands and agreed to appoint the popular Wladyslaw Gomulka as the new prime minister.

text: KũrĨa Indus Valley, ũthii wa na mbere warehetwo ni Bronze Age thĨiniĨ wa gĨcigĨrĨra kĨa northwest India kĨrĨa gĨkoragwo na mabũrũri ta Pakistan, mĨena Ĩmwe ya northwest India na Northeast Afghanistan.
text_en: The Indus Valley Civilization was a Bronze Age civilisation in the northwest Indian subcontinent encompassing most of modern-day Pakistan and some regions in northwest India and northeast Afghanistan.

text: IcigĨrĨrainĨ cia rũũĨ rwa Indus nĨkũo ũthii ũyũ wa na mbere waarĨ na nĨkuo warutire rĨtwa rĨrĨ.
text_en: The civilisation flourished in the basins of the Indus River wherefore it derives its name.

text: Ona gũtwĨka athomi amwe meciragĨria atĨ ũthii ũyũ wa na mbere warĨ kuo icigĨrĨra-inĨ cia rũũĨ rũrĨa rwomĨte rwa Sarasvati, kwoguo wagĨrĨire gwĨto Indus-Sarasvati Civilization, kũrĨa angĨ mawĨtaga Harrapan Civilization kuuma kũrĨ Harrapa, kũndũ kũrĨa kwenjiro rĨa mbere mĨaka ya 1920s.
text_en: Although some scholars speculate that since the civilisation also existed in the basins of the now dried up Sarasvati River, it should be aptly called the Indus-Sarasvati Civilization, while some call it the Harappan Civilization after Harappa, the first of its sites to be excavated in the 1920s.

text: Ni ũndũire wa kĨmbirarũ wa Roman empire wateithĨrĨirie ũthii wa na mbere wa ũrigitani.
text_en: The militaristic nature of the Roman empire aided in the development of medical advances.

text: NdagitarĨ nĨciambĨrĨirie kwandĨkwo nĨ Emperor Augustus na nginya akĨambĨrĨria Roman Medical Corps ya mbere gũteithĨrĨria thuutha wa mbaara.
text_en: Doctors began to be recruited by Emperor Augustus and even formed the first Roman Medical Corps for use in the aftermath of battles.

text: Arigitani a gũthĨnja nĨmaarĨ na ũmenyo wa ndaawa cia kũgonia cigana ũna ta morphine kuuma kwĨ mbegũ cia poppy na scopolamine kuuma kwĨ mbegũ cia herbane.
text_en: Surgeons had knowledge of various sedatives including morphine from extracts of poppy seeds and scopolamine from herbane seeds.

text: NĨmagĨire na ũmenyo mũnene wa gũtinia ciĨga nĨguo kuhonokia arũaru kuuma kũri mĨrimu ta gangrene, tourniquets na arterial clamps nĨguo gũteithĨrĨria thakame gũceera.
text_en: They became proficient at amputation to save patients from gangrene as well as tourniquets and arterial clamps to stem blood flow.

text: Thuutha wa centuries nyingĨ, Roman empire nĨyatũmire kũgĨe na maendereo thĨiniĨ wa ũrigitani na nĨyo kĨambĨrĨria kĨa maũndũ maingĨ marĨa tũũĨ ũmuthĨ.
text_en: Over multiple centuries, the Roman empire led to great gains in the field of medicine and formed much of the knowledge we know today.

text: Pureland origami nĨ origami ĨrĨa Ĩkoragwo na mĨhĨnga mĨingĨ ati no mũkũnjo ũmwe ũngĨthondekwo kwa ihinda rĨmwe, mikũnjo ĨrĨa mĨritũ nditĨkĨrĨtio na mĨkũnjo yoothe no nginya Ĩrore mbere.
text_en: Pureland origami is origami with the restriction that only one fold may be done at a time, more complex folds like reverse folds are not allowed, and all folds have straightforward locations.

text: Yathondekirwo nĨ John Smith mĨaka-inĨ ya 1970s gũteithĨrĨria acũhia arĨa mataarĨ na ũmenyo mũingĨ kana arĨa mataarĨ na mĨtũkĨ ya mooko.
text_en: It was developed by John Smith in the 1970s to help inexperienced folders or those with limited motor skills.

text: Ciana citaũkagwo nĩ maũndũ megainie na ũthutũkania wa rangi marĩ anini na maũndũ maya ma ũthũtũkania nĩ makoragwo mahutanĩtie na mĩtugo.
text_en: Children develop an awareness of race and racial stereotypes quite young and these racial stereotypes affect behavior.

text: Kwa mũhiano, ciana iria ciĩtanagĩo na ndũrĩrĩ iria itarĩ uuge na magakuruhanio na maũndũ ma ũndũire ma maheni makoragwo mategwĩka wega cukuru na mekaga uuru cukuru-inĩ marĩkia guthoma ũhoro wa gũkuruhanio na maũndũ ma ũnduire ma maheni marĩa metanĩtio na ndurĩrĩ ciao.
text_en: For instance, children who identify with a racial minority that is stereotyped as not doing well in school tend to not do well in school once they learn about the stereotype associated with their race.

text: Rũrenda rũrĩa rwa gatatũ kũmenyekana mũno nĩ ta MySpace bũrũri-inĩ wa Amerika, na rũtũmagĩrwo nĩ arũmĩrĩri matanyihĩirie millioni mĩrongo ĩtano na inya.
text_en: MySpace is the third most popular website used in the United States and has 54 million profiles currently.

text: Ngenda ta icio nĩ irarũmbũyanio nacio mũno, na makiria ciikaro inĩ cia mathomo.
text_en: These websites have gotten a lot of attention, especially in the education setting.

text: Kwĩna maũndũ mega metanĩtio na rũrenda, ta guthondeka irathi mĩtamboini kũrĩa mathomo maraheano na njĩra cia mbica, video,  maandĩko na mangĩ ta macio.
text_en: There are positive aspects to these websites, which include, being able to easily setup a class page which can include blogs, videos, photos, and other features.

text: Page ĩno no ĩkinyĩrĩke na ihenya na njĩra ya kũheana rũrenda o rũmwe, ũndu ũrĩa ũhotithagia kũririkana kwa na ihenya, na gũteithia arutwo arĩa mena thĩna wa gũtũmira keyboard kana gũthondeka maritwa.
text_en: This page can easily be accessed by providing just one web address, which makes it easy to remember and easy to type in for students who may have trouble using the keyboard or with spelling.

text: No ĩthondeko nĩguo ĩhũthie mathomo, na cĩĩkĩro marangi na kũringana na wendi wa ene.
text_en: It can be customized to make it easy to read and also with as much or little color as desired.

text: Attention Deficit disorder " nĩ mũrimũ wa hakiri ũrĩa dariri ciake cikoragwo ta impulsivity, kũgiĩka, gũthumbũka na hyperactivity kana hinya mũingĩ".
text_en: Attention Deficit Disorder "is a neurological syndrome whose classic defining triad of symptoms including impulsivity, distractibility, and hyperactivity or excess energy".

text: Ti kũremwo nĩ gũthoma no nĩ murimũ wa kwaga ũhoti wa gũthoma; "ũgwataga gĩcunjĩ kĩa 3 nginya 5 harĩ igana gĩa ciana ciothe, na no makorwo marĩ aingĩ ta mirioni 2 thĩiniĩ wa America. "
text_en: It is not a learning disability, it is a learning disorder; it "affects 3 to 5 percent of all children, perhaps as many as 2 million American children".

text: Ciana irĩa ikoragwo na ADD nĩ ikoragwo na ũritũ harĩ maũndũ ta wĩra wa cukuru, no nomahote kũiga meciria maao handũ maũndũ marĩa makenagirira magĩka ta gũthaka mĩthako, kũona gatuni iria mendete mũno kana kwandĩka raini mategwĩkĩra marũri.
text_en: Children with ADD have a hard time focusing on things like school work, but they can concentrate on things they enjoy doing like playing games or watching their favorite cartoons or writing sentences without punctuation.

text: Ciana ici mahinda kwa mahinda nĩciĩkoraga thĩna-inĩ tondũ " Wakwĩingĩria mĩtũgo-inĩ  mĩũru, kwĩingiria mbaraa-inĩ, na kũhe watho ihinda iritũ" nĩguo gucanjamũra hakiri ciao tondũ hakiri ciao citingĩcanjamurwo na njĩra cia kawaida.
text_en: These children tend to get into a lot of trouble, because they "engage in risky behaviors, get into fights, and challenge authority" in order to stimulate their brain, since their brain can not be stimulated by normal methods.

text: ADD nĩthũkagia ũrata wao na andũ angĩ tondũ ciana ingĩ itingĩhota gũtaũkĩrwo nĩkĩĩ gĩtũmaga meke maũndũ ũrĩa mekaga kana gũtamũka ũrĩa matamũkaga kana atĩ ũgima wao nĩ ũrĩ ũtiganu.
text_en: ADD affects relationships with other peers because other children can not understand why they act the way that they do or why they spell they way they do or that their maturity level is different.

text: Hindi iria uhoti wa kugia ugi na guthoma wacenjiriena njira ta iria igwetetwo hau iguru, gitina gia uthimi kiria ugi wagitwo nakio ugicenjia.
text_en: As the ability to obtain knowledge and to learn changed in such a way as mentioned above the base rate at which knowledge was obtained changed.

text: Njĩra ya kũngania ũhoro yaarĩ ngũrani. Ũndũ wa mũndũ gũkorwo na bata wa kũririkana nĩwathirire, no uhoti wa kũririkana maandiko ũgĩkĩĩrĩrwo mũno.
text_en: The approach to obtaining information was different. No longer did pressure reside within individual recall, but the ability to recall text became more of a focus.

text: Renaissance nĩyatũmire kũgĩe na ũgarũrũku mũnene harĩ njĩra cia gũthomithia na kuhĩtũkia ũũgĩ.
text_en: In essence, the Renaissance made a significant change in the approach to learning and the dissemination of knowledge.

text: Ũtiganu na primates, hominids itihũthĩraga moko maacio kuuma handũ hamwe nginya harĩa hangĩ kana gũkuua ũritũ kana gũcuha mĩtĩ-inĩ.
text_en: Unlike other primates, hominids no longer use their hands in locomotion or bearing weight or swinging through the trees.

text: Guoko na kũgũrũ gwa nũgũ nĩgũkuhanĩrĩirie  harĩ ũnene na ũraihu, kuonania guoko kũhũthĩkaga gũkua ũritũ rĩrĩa ĩrathiĩ na moko.
text_en: The chimpanzee's hand and foot are similar in size and length, reflecting the hand's use for bearing weight in knuckle walking.

text: Guoko gwa mũndũ nĩ kũnini gũkĩra kũgũrũ, na gũkoragwo na mahĩndĩ marũngarũ.
text_en: The human hand is shorter than the foot, with straighter phalanges.

text: Mahĩndĩ ma moko marĩa mena ũkũrũ wa mĩaka mirĩoni igĩrĩ nginya ithatũ monanagia gũcenjia kwa moko kuuma gũthiĩ nginyagia kũruta wĩra.
text_en: Fossil hand bones two million to three million years old reveal this shift in specialization of the hand from locomotion to manipulation.

text: Andũ amwe metĩkĩtie atĩ gũkorwo na iroto nyingĩ lucid iria nĩ  artificially induced no kũnogie mũndũ mũno.
text_en: Some people believe that experiencing many artificially induced lucid dreams often enough can be very exhausting.

text: Gĩtũmi kĩnene kĩa maũndũ kũhanĩka ũguo nĩ maumĩrĩra ma iroto lucid ikĩnenehia ũraihũ wa ihinda gatagatĩ ga REM states.
text_en: The main reason for this phenomenon is the result of the lucid dreams expanding the length of time between REM states.

text: Na ũnyihu wa REMs harĩ ũtukũ, ũndũ ũyũ rĩrĩa ũgĩaga toro wa ma na mwĩrĩ waku ũkahona na ũkagĩa na maũndũ maĩganu ma gutuĩka thĩĩna.
text_en: With fewer REMs per night, this state in which you experience actual sleep and your body recovers becomes infrequent enough to become a problem.

text: Ũndũ ũyũ ũnogagia mũndũ ota ũrĩa ũngĩũkĩra thuutha wa ndagĩka mĩrongo iirĩ kana mĩrongo ĩtatũ kwĩrorera TV.
text_en: This is just as exhausting as if you were to wake up every twenty or thirty minutes and watch TV.

text: Maumĩrĩra maringanaga na maita marĩa hakiri ciaku igeragia kũrota lucidly o utukũ.
text_en: The effect is dependent on how often your brain attempts to lucidly dream per night.

text: Maũndũ matiathire wega kuuma o kĩambĩrĩria kũrĩ Aitariano arĩa maari Rũgongo rwa Afirika. Kahinda ini ka kiumia kĩmwe thutha wa Itari gutangatha mbaara kurĩ mweri wa gatandatũ 10, 1940, mbatu ya Ngeretha ya Hussars 11 niyegwatiire Fort Capuzzo kuu Libya.
text_en: Things did not go well for the Italians in North Africa almost from the start. Within a week of Italy's declaration of war on June 10, 1940, the British 11th Hussars had seized Fort Capuzzo in Libya.

text: Kuhĩtũkira ihithũkĩra Irathĩro rĩa Bardia, Ngeretha niyanyitire mĩgwate General Lastucci ũrĩa warĩ Inginia mũnene wa mbatũ ya Itari rĩa Ikũmi..
text_en: In an ambush east of Bardia, the British captured the Italian Tenth Army's Engineer-in-Chief, General Lastucci.

text: Kũrĩ mweri wa gatandatũ 28, Marshal Italo Balbo, ũrĩa warĩ Gavana Mũnene wa Libya na mũgai wa Mussolini nĩoragirwo nĩ mbũtũ ciao o hĩndĩ akinya Tobruk.
text_en: On June 28, Marshal Italo Balbo, the Governor-General of Libya and apparent heir to Mussolini, was killed by friendly fire while landing in Tobruk.

text: Mũthako wa kĩrĩu wa fencing ũthakagwo ngathĩ-inĩ nyingĩ kuuma kũrĩ arutwo a university nginya mathako ma professionals na macindano ma Olympic.
text_en: The modern sport of fencing is played at many levels, from students learning at a university to professional and Olympic competition.

text: Mũthako ũyũ ũthakagwo nĩ andũ eerĩ, mũthaki ũmwe akĩgeria kũrũnda ũrĩa ũngĩ.
text_en: The sport is primarily played in a duel format, one fencer dueling another.

text: Ngobu nĩ mũthako ũrĩa athaki mahũthagira irabu kũgũtha mĩbira gũtonyia marima-ini.
text_en: Golf is a game in which players use clubs to hit balls into holes.

text: Marima ikũmi na manana nĩmo mathakagwo mũthiũrũrũko-inĩ wa kawaida, athaki mambagĩrĩria irima-inĩ rĩa mbere na kũrĩkĩrĩria irima-inĩ rĩa ikũmi na kanana.
text_en: Eighteen holes are played during a regular round, with players usually starting on the first hole on the course and finishing on the eighteenth.

text: Mũthaki ũrĩa ũkoragwo na magũtha manini biũ, kana swing nini cia kĩrabu kũrĩkia mũthiũrũrũko nĩwe mũhotani.
text_en: The player who takes the fewest strokes, or swings of the club, to complete the course wins.

text: Mũthako ũyũ ũthakagĩrwo nyeki-inĩ, na nyeki ĩrĩa ĩkoragwo hakuhĩ na irima ĩrengagwo ĩrĩ nini mũno na ĩĩtagwo green.
text_en: The game is played on grass, and the grass around the hole is mown shorter and called the green.

text: Nogũkorwo mũthemba ũrĩa ũĩkaine mũno wa ugendi nĩ ũrĩa ũĩkaine na thabarĩ: ũgendi wa gwĩkenia.
text_en: Perhaps the most common type of tourism is what most people associate with traveling: Recreation tourism.

text: Rĩrĩ nĩ hĩndĩ ĩrĩa andũ mathiaga kũndũ gũtiganĩte na mũtũũrĩre wao wa o mũthenya kũhũrũkia hakiri na gwĩkenia.
text_en: This is when people go to a place that is very different from their regular day-to-day life to relax and have fun.

text: Beaches, theme parks na camp grounds kaingĩ nĩkuo kũndũ kũrĩa gũceragwo mũno nĩ agendi a gwĩkenia.
text_en: Beaches, theme parks and camp grounds are often the most common places frequented by recreational tourists.

text: Angĩkorwo mworoto wa gũceera handũ hamwe nĩ kũmenya ũndũire na maũndũ maho ma tene, ũgendi ũyũ ũĩkaine ta ũgendi wa kĩndũire.
text_en: If the objective of one’s visit to a particular place is to get to know its history and culture then this type of tourism is known as cultural tourism.

text: Agendi nomacerere kũndũ gũtiganĩte thĩiniĩ wa bũrũri ũmwe kana no matue itua gũcerera handũ hamwe.
text_en: Tourists may visit different landmarks of a particular country or they may simply opt to focus on just one area.

text: Nao athani kuma bũrũri ũngĩ mona mawĩko macio, magĩtia ũteithio.
text_en: The Colonists, seeing this activity, had also called for reinforcements.

text: Mbirarũ cia ũteithia wa mũhari wa mbere ciarĩ ikundi cia mbirarũ cia mbere na gatatũ ithondeketwo nĩ jeshi magana merĩ cia New Hampshire, itongoretio nĩ colonels John Stark na James Reed ( arĩa rĩa mũico matuĩkĩre generals).
text_en: Troops reinforcing the forward positions included the 1st and 3rd New Hampshire regiments of 200 men, under Colonels John Stark and James Reed (both later became generals).

text: Andũ arũme a Stark makĩoya icigĩrĩra iria ciarĩ rũgiri-inĩ mũico-inĩ wa icigo cia rũgongo iria ciarĩ cia athani acio.
text_en: Stark's men took positions along the fence on the north end of the Colonist's position.

text: Rĩrĩa makũmbĩ manini mathondekire mwanya rũũĩ-inĩ rwa Mystic River gũkĩrania mwena wa rũgongo wa Peninsula, makĩongerera rũgiri na ihenya na rũthingo rũkuhĩ rwa ihiga mũthia-inĩ wa rũgongo wa maaĩ ma gĩcũa-inĩ.
text_en: When low tide opened a gap along the Mystic River along the northeast of the peninsula, they quickly extended the fence with a short stone wall to the north ending at the water's edge on a small beach.

text: Gridley na Stark makĩiga gĩthũkĩ kĩarĩ kĩa fiti igana rĩmwe (mita mĩrongo ĩtatũ) mbere ya rũgiri na makiuga gũtirĩ wagĩrĩirwo nĩ gũtũrĩkia nginyagia andũ a kũu mambe mahetũke.
text_en: Gridley or Stark placed a stake about 100 feet (30 m) in front of the fence and ordered that no one fire until the regulars passed it.

text: Mũbango wa Americans wehokete kũambiriria tharikira bacirire kumana na miena itatũ itiganite.
text_en: The American plan relied on launching coordinated attacks from three different directions.

text: Mũnene wa mbũtũ John Cadwalder ambagĩrĩria tharĩkĩra ya kũgarũrania arongoreirie mbũtũ cia British kũu Bordentown, nĩ getha ahingĩrĩrie ũteithio o wothe kuma nanja.
text_en: General John Cadwalder would launch a diversionary attack against the British garrison at Bordentown, in order to block off any reinforcements.

text: Mũnene wa mbũtũ nĩwe James Ewing atwaraga itoi ciake gukĩrania rũũĩ rwa Trenton Ferry, magetahĩra ndaraca igũrũ rĩa Assunpink Greek na akagitĩra mbũtũ cia thũ kũra.
text_en: General James Ewing would take 700 militia across the river at Trenton Ferry, seize the bridge over the Assunpink Creek and prevent any enemy troops from escaping.

text: Mbũtũ ĩrĩa nene ya gũtharĩkĩra yarĩ ya arũme ngiri igĩrĩ na magana mana yakĩraga rũũĩ mairo kenda rũgongo rwa Trenton, magacoka makagayana ikundi igĩrĩ, ĩmwe ĩ rungu rwa Green na ĩngĩ ĩmwe ĩ rungu rwa Sullivan, nĩ getha mambĩrĩrie tharĩkĩra mbere ya gukĩte.
text_en: The main assault force of 2,400 men would cross the river nine miles north of Trenton, and then split into two groups, one under Greene and one under Sullivan, in order to launch a pre-dawn attack.

text: Na mogarũrũku kuma harĩ gacunjĩ kamwe ka inya nginya nuthu ya mairo iteng'era, ihenya rĩtuikaga rĩa bata hanini na kũmĩrĩria gũgatuika kwa bata makĩria.
text_en: With the change from the quarter to the half mile run, speed becomes of much less importance and endurance becomes an absolute necessity.

text: Hatarĩ nganja ateng'eri a nuthu ya mairo a kĩrathi kĩa mbere, mũndũ ũngĩhũra ihinda rĩa dagĩka igĩrĩ, no nginya akorwo na ihenya riega, no ũmĩrĩru no nginyagia ũrĩmĩwro na njĩra ciothe.
text_en: Of course a first-class half-miler, a man who can beat two minutes, must be possessed of a fair amount of speed, but endurance must be cultivated at all hazards.

text: ũteng'eri wa gũkĩrania matũra-inĩ hĩndĩ ya heho, ĩtukanĩtio na mathako thĩinĩ wa nyũmba ya mathako ma kũnogora mĩĩrĩ ma mwena wa naigũrũ wa mwĩrĩ, nĩmo mega mũno ma kwĩharĩrĩria ihinda rĩa gũteng'era.
text_en: Some cross country running during the winter, combined with gymnasium work for the upper part of the body, is the best preparation for the running season.

text: Mĩtugo mĩega ya mĩrĩre ĩ ike ndĩngĩruta maumĩrĩra mega ma mĩthakĩre, no noĩteithie na hinya ũgima wa ateng'eri arĩa mena mĩaka mĩnini.
text_en: Proper nutritional practices alone cannot generate elite performances, but they can significantly affect young athletes' overall wellness.

text: Gũikara na ũgima mwega wa mwĩrĩ na hinya ũigananĩirie, kwĩruta mĩtugo mĩega ya ũnyui wa mai, na gũtaũkĩro nĩ maũndũ maingĩ meigiĩ mĩtugo ya kũongerera indo ingĩ no ĩteithie ateng'eri kũongerera mũthakĩre na kũongerera mũkenere wao harĩ mathako mao.
text_en: Maintaining a healthy energy balance, practicing effective hydration habits, and understanding the various aspects of supplementation practices can help athletes improve their performance and increase their enjoyment of the sport.

text: ũteng'eri wa ihenya rĩa ũraihu wa gatagatĩ ti mũthako ũrĩ goro mũno ũringithanĩtio na ĩyo ĩngĩ; no kũrĩ ũguo, nĩ gũkoragwo na mawoni matarĩ ma ũma makonainie na mwĩcirĩrie mũrũ wa indo nini iria ibatarĩkanaga kũnyita itemi.
text_en: Middle distance running is a relatively inexpensive sport; however, there are many misconceptions regarding the few pieces of equipment required to participate.

text: Indo no igũrwo kũringana na ũrĩa irabatarĩkana, no nyingĩ igakorwo itarĩ na maumĩrĩra kana magakorwo me manini harĩ mũthakĩre.
text_en: Products can be purchased as needed, but most will have little or no real impact on performance.

text: Athaki no maigue nĩ marenda kĩndũ ona angĩkorwo gĩtiramahe ũguni o wothe.
text_en: Athletes may feel that they prefer a product even when it provides no real benefits.

text: Atomu nĩ ciĩciragĩrio ta arĩ imwe cia mũthingi ũrĩa ũthondekete indo ciothe.
text_en: The atom can be considered to be one of the fundamental building blocks of all matter.

text: Nĩ rũhonge rũritũ rũrĩa rũkoragwo, kũringana na kĩonereria kĩhũthie kĩa Bohr, rũkoragwo na nucleus gatagatĩ na rũthiũrũrũkagwo nĩ electrons, iria ikoragwo ihana ta thĩ iria ithiũrũrũkaga riũa. Ona mbica 1.1
text_en: Its a very complex entity which consists, according to a simplified Bohr model, of a central nucleus orbited by electrons, somewhat similar to planets orbiting the sun - see Figure 1.1.

text: Nucleus ikoragwo na particles igĩrĩ, neutron na protons.
text_en: The nucleus consists of two particles - neutrons and protons.

text: Protons ikoragwo na charge positive, nacio neutrons igakorwo itarĩ na charge. Electrons ikoragwo na charge negative.
text_en: Protons have a positive electric charge while neutrons have no charge. The electrons have a negative electric charge.

text: Kũrora arĩa magurarĩtio nĩ ũgwati, no nginya ũthuthurie hau ũgwati wonekeire kũmenyerera ũgitĩri waku.
text_en: To Check the victim, you must first survey the scene to ensure your safety.

text: Nĩ ũrabatara kũmenya arĩa mahutĩtio harĩa marĩ ũgĩthiĩ harĩa marĩ na rĩonereria rĩothe rĩa ũgwati.
text_en: You need to notice the victim's position as you approach him or her and any automatic red flags.

text: ũngĩgurario ũkĩgeria gũteithia, no ũteithagĩrĩria gũthũkia maũndũ.
text_en: If you get hurt trying to help, you may only serve to make matters worse.

text: ũthuthuria ũkĩona atĩ mũrimũ wa gũtangĩka meciria, guoya na gwĩcirĩria maũndũ moru no mahanĩke nĩ yanyitithanĩtie ũkuruhanu gatagatĩ ka ruo na wonje harĩ andũ arĩa makoragwo makĩigua ruo mũgongo mwena wa thĩ.
text_en: The study found that depression, fear and catastrophising mediated the relationship between pain and disability in lower back pain sufferers.

text: No maumĩrĩra ma mũrimu wa gwĩtigĩra maũndũ moru gwĩkĩka, tiga mũrimũ wa gũtangĩka meciria na guoya ibataranagio mũbango wa tabarĩra bange ya PA iria ciĩkagwo o kiumia.
text_en: Only the effects of catastrophizing, not depression and fear was conditional of regular weekly structured PA sessions.

text: Arĩa manyitaga itemi maũndũ inĩ macio kaingĩ nĩ mabataraga kũnyitĩrĩwro mĩena-inĩ ya meciria moru ma ruo kũonania ũtigithũkanu wa ruo rũtangĩhona na kũigua ũru harĩ mũthiĩre wa mwĩrĩ.
text_en: Those participating in regular activity required more support in terms of negative perception of pain distinguishing the differences of chronic pain and discomfort feel from normal physical movement.

text: Kũona, kana ũhoti wa kũona ũringanaga na ciĩga cia kũona iria ikoragwo mũtabarire-inĩ ũcio wa kũona kana maitho.
text_en: Vision, or the ability to see depends on visual system sensory organs or eyes.

text: Gũkoragwo na mĩũmbĩre mĩingĩ ĩtiganĩte ya maitho, ĩrĩa ũritũ wa mũmbĩre wa mo ũringanaga na mabataro ma indo ciĩ muoyo.
text_en: There are many different constructions of eyes, ranging in complexity depending on the requirements of the organism.

text: Mũmbĩre ũtiganĩte nĩ ũkoragwo na ũhoti mwanya, na monaga wave-lengths itiganĩte na magakorwo na ikĩro cia ũhoti wa kũona itiganĩte, na no mabataraga hinya wa gũtaũra ũtiganĩte nĩ getha gũtaũkĩro nĩ kĩrĩa kĩingĩrire na namba itiganĩte kũruta wĩra ũrĩa ciagĩrĩire.
text_en: The different constructions have different capabilities, are sensitive to different wave-lengths and have differing degrees of acuity, also they require different processing to make sense of the input and different numbers to work optimally.

text: Mũingĩ nĩ ũcokanĩrĩria wa indo ciĩ ciĩga cia mũthemba ũmwe kuma gĩcigo kĩheane.
text_en: A population is the collection of organisms of a particular species within a given geographic area.

text: Rĩrĩa andũ othe harĩ mũingĩ mahanaine kũringana na maũthĩ maroneka metagwo monomorphic.
text_en: When all individuals in a population are identical with regard to a particular phenotypic trait they are known as monomorphic.

text: Rĩrĩa andũ monania ũtigithũkanu mũingĩ harĩ maũthĩ furani makoragwo marĩ polymorphic.
text_en: When the individuals show several variants of a particular trait they are polymorphic.

text: Mbũtũ cia thigiriri iria cikaraga gĩcigĩrĩra kĩmwe nĩ imacaga na igathondeka itara mahinda-inĩ matiganĩte ona cio.
text_en: Army ant colonies march and nest in different phases as well.

text: Mahinda-inĩ ma gũthama, mbũtũ cia thigiriri nĩ imacaga ũtukũ na ikarũgama kwamba hema kũrĩ mũthenya.
text_en: In the nomadic phase, army ants march at night and stop to camp during the day.

text: Nyamũ icio ciikarĩte gĩcigĩrĩra kĩmwe ciambagĩrĩria ihinda rĩa gũthama rĩrĩa irio iria ciĩho ciambĩrĩria kũnyiha. Ihinda-inĩ rĩrĩ, koronĩ ĩno nĩ yambagĩrĩria gũthondeka itara iria icenjagio o mũthenya.
text_en: The colony begins a nomadic phase when available food has decreased. During this phase, the colony makes temporary nests that are changed everyday.

text: O ithama rĩmwe rĩa ũru na ũthũkangia mũingĩ kana kũmaci kũu gũikaraga gwa kahinda gakuhĩrĩirie thikũ ikũmi na mũgwanja.
text_en: Each of these nomadic rampages or marches lasts for approximately 17 days.

text: Kahengereti nĩ kĩĩ? Kiugo cell kiumĩte harĩ rĩtwa rĩa kĩ Latin nĩrĩo "cella" riugaga "rumu nini" na rĩrĩa rĩatũmĩrirwo rita rĩa mbere nĩ andũ arĩa matũmĩraga mikroscopu kũona mũbangĩre wa cork.
text_en: What is a cell? The word cell comes from the Latin word "cella", meaning "small room", and it was first coined by a microscopist observing the structure of cork.

text: Kahengereca nĩko kĩndũ kĩmwe kĩa mũthingi harĩ indo ciothe ciĩ muoyo, na indo ciothe ciĩ ciĩga nĩ ithondekagwo nĩ kahengereca kamwe kana makĩria.
text_en: The cell is the basic unit of all living things, and all organisms are composed of one or more cells.

text: Tũhengereca tũkoragwo twĩ twa mũthingi na twa bata harĩ ũthuthuria wa ũtũro, na ũma nĩ atĩ, kaingĩ twĩtagwo ta "mahiga ma gwaka ũtũro".
text_en: Cells are so basic and critical to the study of life, in fact, that they are often referred to as "the building blocks of life".

text: Mũtabarĩre wa mĩkiha ya gũtwara ũhoro ũigaga ũigananĩirie kũringana na marĩa marigicĩirie na njĩra ya gũtũma nerve impulses mwĩrĩ wothe kũiga ũthii wa thakama ũikarĩte wega na ũtegũthumbũro.
text_en: The Nervous System maintains homeostasis by sending nerve impulses through out the body to keep the flow of blood going as well as undisturbed.

text: Nerve impulses icio no itumwo na ihenya mwĩrĩ wothe iria iteithagia kũiga mwĩrĩ kũraihu na ũgwati kana ũndũ ũngĩrehe ũgwati.
text_en: These nerve impulses can be sent so quickly throughout the body which helps keep the body safe from any potential threat.

text: Tornadoes nĩ imunyaga mĩtĩ, ikambũrania ibao kuma nyũmba-inĩ na ikombũkia ngaari rĩera-inĩ. Iria ikoragwo na haro njũru nĩ gacunjĩ ka igĩrĩ harĩ igana na nĩ ciikaraga makĩria ma mathaa matatũ.
text_en: Tornadoes strike a small area compared to other violent storms, but they can destroy everything in their path.

text: Tornadoes nĩ imunyaga mĩtĩ, ikambũrania boards kuma nyũmba-inĩ na ikombũkia ngaari rĩera-inĩ. Iria ikoragwo na haro njũru nĩ gacunjĩ ka igĩrĩ harĩ igana na nĩ ciikaraga makĩria ya mathaa matatũ.
text_en: Tornadoes uproot trees, rip boards from buildings, and fling cars up into the sky. The most violent two percent of tornadoes last more than three hours.

text: Ihuhũkanio icio nene nĩ ikoragwo na huho cia nginya kiromita magana mana ma mĩrongo ĩnana harĩ ithaa (mita igana rĩmwe rĩa mĩrongo ĩtatũ na ithatũ harĩ seconds; mairo magana matatũ harĩ ithaa).
text_en: These monster storms have winds up to 480 km/h (133 m/s; 300 mph).

text: Andũ makoretwo magĩtũmĩra icicio cia kũnenehia indo iria ironwo ngiri na ngiri cia mĩaka.
text_en: Humans have been making and using lenses for magnification for thousands and thousands of years.

text: Ona kũrĩ ũguo, telescope ya mbere ya ma ciathondekeirwo Europe mũthia-inĩ wa century ya ikũmi na gatandatũ.
text_en: However, the first true telescopes were made in Europe in the late 16th century.

text: Telescopes ici ciatũmagĩra mũnyitithanio wa icicio igĩrĩ cia lenses gũtũma indo ciĩ kũraihu cionekana ciĩ hakuhĩ na ciĩ nene.
text_en: These telescopes used a combination of two lenses to make distant objects appear both nearer and larger.

text: ũkoroku na kwĩyenda ũrĩkoragwo na ithui hĩndĩ ciothe, na nĩguo ũnyitaniri ũhana atĩ rĩrĩa aingĩ marateithĩka nĩ kũrĩkoragwo hĩndĩ ciothe na kũgĩa makĩria kahinda-inĩ kanini na njĩra ya  gwĩka maũndũ na wĩyendi.
text_en: Greed and selfishness will always be with us and it is the nature of cooperation that when the majority benefit there will always be more to gain in the short term by acting selfishly

text: mwĩhoko nĩ atĩ, andũ aingĩ nĩ marĩmenya atĩ itua rĩrĩa rĩao rĩega rĩa kahinda karaihu nĩ kũrutithania wĩra na arĩa angĩ.
text_en: Hopefully, most people will realise that their long term best option is to work together with others.

text: Andũ aingĩ marotagĩra mũthenya ũrĩa andũ magathiĩ njata-inĩ ingĩ magathuthurie thĩ ĩngĩ, andũ amwe nĩ marigagwo nĩ kĩĩ kĩ nakũu nja na amwe magetĩkia atĩ ageni kana indo ingĩ ciĩ muoyo no cikorwo cikaraga thĩ ingĩ.
text_en: Many people dream of the day when humans can travel to another star and explore other worlds, some people wonder what's out there some belive that aliens or other life may live on another plant.

text: No ningĩ, ũndũ ũyũ angĩkorwo nĩ ũgekĩka nokũhoteteke ũndũ ũcio ndũngĩkĩka ha kahinda karaihu mũno, njata nĩ ikoragwo inyaganĩte atĩ nĩ mairo tririoni nyingĩ gatagatĩ ka njata iria ikuhanĩrĩirie.
text_en: But, if this ever does happen probably won't happen for a very long time. The stars are so spread out that there are trillions of miles between stars that are "neighbors".

text: Nokorwo mũthenya ũmwe, tũcũkũrũ twakũ nĩ tũkarũgama igũrũ rĩa thĩ cia alliens makĩgeria gwĩciria ũhoro wa aguuka a cio a tene.
text_en: Maybe one day, your great grandchildren will be standing atop an alien world wondering about their ancient ancestors?

text: Nyamũ ikoragwo ithondeketwo na tũhengereta tũingĩ. Irĩaga indo na igacithĩa thĩinĩ. Nyamũ nyingĩ no ithiĩ.
text_en: Animals are made of many cells. They eat things and digest them inside. Most animals can move.

text: No nyamũ ikoragwo na hakiri (Ona akoro to nyamũ ciothe ikoragwo; Jellyfish, kwa mũhiano, itikoragwo na hakiri).
text_en: Only animals have brains (though not even all animals do; jellyfish, for example, do not have brains).

text: Nyamũ cionekanaga kũndũ gũothe thĩ yothe. Ni cienjaga thĩ, igatubĩra iria-inĩ, na ikombũkĩra igũrũ.
text_en: Animals are found all over the earth. They dig in the ground, swim in the oceans, and fly in the sky.

text: Karengeta nĩko gakoragwo ge kanini mũno mũmbĩre-inĩ na mũrutĩre wa wĩra harĩ indo iria ciothe ciĩ muoyo.
text_en: A cell is the smallest structural and functional unit of a living (things) organism.

text: Cell riumaga kũrĩ rĩtwa rĩa Latin rĩrĩa riugaga rumu nini.
text_en: Cell comes from the Latin word cella which means small room.

text: ũngĩrora indo iria ciĩ muoyo rungu rwa microscope, no wone ikoragwo ithondeketwo na mĩena ĩna ĩiganaaine kana mĩbira.
text_en: If you look at living things under a microscope, you will see that they are made of small squares or balls.

text: Robert Hooke, mũtaramu wa maũndũ ma biology kuuma Ngeretha, onire kĩndũ kĩa mĩena ĩna ĩiganaaine harĩ gĩkundi gĩa tũhengereta na agĩtũmĩra microscope.
text_en: Robert Hooke, a biologist from England, saw small squares in cork with a microscope.

text: Ciahanaga rumu. Arĩ mũndũ wa mbere kũona tũhengereta tũkuũ.
text_en: They looked like rooms. He was the first person to observe dead cells

text: Elements na compound no icenjie kuma state ĩmwe nginya ĩngĩ itegũcenjia.
text_en: Elements and compounds can move from one state to another and not change.

text: Nitrogen ĩta rĩera ĩkoragwo na maũthĩ mahanaine na nitrogen ĩ maaĩ. Gũkorwo ĩringũkĩte nĩ gũtũmaga ĩkorwo ĩ nditũ no molecules no cio.
text_en: Nitrogen as a gas still has the same properties as liquid nitrogen. The liquid state is denser but the molecules are still the same.

text: Maaĩ nĩ mũhiano ũngĩ. Maaĩ me compound nĩ mathondekagwo nĩ atoms igĩrĩ cia hydrogen na ĩmwe ya oxygen.
text_en: Water is another example. The compound water is made up of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

text: Makoragwo na mũmbĩre ũmwe wa mũbangĩre wa molecules kana wĩ mũthemba-inĩ wa gas, liquid kana solid.
text_en: It has the same molecular structure whether it is a gas, liquid, or solid.

text: Ona akorwo state no icenjie, chemical states itigaraga ihanaine.
text_en: Although its physical state may change, its chemical state remains the same.

text: Mathaa nĩ kĩndũ gĩtũthiũrũrũkĩirie kũndũ guothe, na mahutagia ũndũ wothe tũreka, no nĩ hinya kũmataũkwo.
text_en: Time is something that is all around us, and affects everything we do, yet is difficult to understand.

text: Mathaa nĩmakoretwo mathometwo nĩ athomi a ndini, a ũũgĩ wa andũ na a gĩ-sayansi handũ-inĩ ha makiri ma mĩaka.
text_en: Time has been studied by religious, philosophical, and scientific scholars for thousands of years.

text: Tũmenyaga ũhoro wa mathaa ta kũrũmanĩrĩra kwa maũndũ makĩhĩtũka kuuma marĩa magooka kũhĩtũkĩra ma rĩu na ma tene.
text_en: We experience time as a series of events passing from the future through the present to the past.

text: Ningĩ mathaa nĩ ũrĩa tũringithanagia ihinda (ũraihu) rĩa maundũ marĩa mareekĩka.
text_en: Time is also how we compare the duration (length) of events.

text: No wĩkĩre rũũri kũhĩtũka kwa ihinda wee mwene na njĩra ya kũrora ũrĩa maũndũ marĩa mecookagĩra marecookera. Ũndũ wa gwĩcookera nĩ ũndũ ũrĩa ũhaanĩkaga rĩngĩ na rĩngĩ maita maingĩ.
text_en: You can mark the passing of time yourself by observing the repetition of a cyclical event. A cyclical event is something that happens again and again regularly.

text: Kambiuta cia ũmũthĩ ihũthĩkaga gũtwarithĩrĩria mbica na thenema.
text_en: Computers today are used to manipulate pictures and videos.

text: Mũceeracerio wa mbica na njĩra ya kĩriga kĩnene no ũthondekwo kambiuta-inĩ, na mũceeracerio ũyũ wa mbica nĩũrathiĩ na mbere kũhũthĩka thĩ-inĩ wa TV na thenema.
text_en: Sophisticated animations can be constructed on computers, and this kind of animation is increasingly being used in television and films.

text: Rwĩmbo kaingĩ rwandĩkagwo ũkĩhũthĩra kambiuta cia kĩriga kĩnene nĩguo kũbanga na gũtukania mĩgambo hamwe.
text_en: Music is often recorded using sophisticated computers to process and mix sounds together.

text: Kwa ihinda iraaya hĩndĩ ya Magana-inĩ ma mĩaka ya ikumi na kenda na ya mĩrongo ĩĩrĩ, gwetĩkĩtio atĩ aikari a mbere a New Zealand maarĩ andũ a Maori, arĩa maahĩtaga nyoni nene ciĩtagwo moas.
text_en: For a long time during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, it was believed the first inhabitants of New Zealand were the Maori people, who hunted giant birds called moas.

text: Ũrutani ũyũ nĩwacookire gũthegeithia rĩĩciria rĩa atĩ andũ a Maori maathamire kuuma Polynesia thĩ-inĩ wa Mũtoongoro Mũnene wa Meeri na makĩoya New Zealand kuuma kũrĩ andũ a Moriori, magĩĩthegea ta andũ a kũrĩma.
text_en: The theory then established the idea that the Maori people migrated from Polynesia in a Great Fleet and took New Zealand from the Moriori, establishing an agricultural society.

text: No ĩndĩ, ũira mwerũ ũroonania atĩ andũ a Moriori maarĩ gĩkundi kĩa a-Maori a thĩ nyũmũ arĩa maathamire kuuma New Zealand magĩthiĩ Icigĩrĩra-inĩ cia Chatham, magĩkũria ũndũire wao ene wĩkũũraine, wa thaayũ.
text_en: However, new evidence suggests that the Moriori were a group of mainland Maori who migrated from New Zealand to the Chatham Islands, developing their own distinctive, peaceful culture.

text: Ningĩ nĩ kwarĩ na rũrĩrĩ rũngĩ kũu icigĩrĩra-inĩ cia Chatham nao aya maarĩ Maori arĩa maathamire makiuma New Zealand.
text_en: There was also another tribe on the Chatham islands these were Maori who migrated away from New Zealand.

text: Meĩĩtaga Moriori nĩ kwarĩ na nditimũrano nini na mũthia-inĩ, andũ a Mariori makĩninwo.
text_en: They called themselves the Moriori there were a few skirmishes and in the end, the Moriori were wiped out

text: Andũ kĩũmbe arĩa makuruhanĩte handũ-inĩ ha makũmi maigana ũna ma mĩaka nĩmatũteithirie gũkenera mahinya maitũ na wendo wa maũndũ o tũkĩroraga tũtekwĩhitha mooritũ o na nginya maremwo.
text_en: Individuals who had been involved for several decades helped us appreciate our strengths and passions while candidly assessing difficulties and even failures.

text: Hĩndĩ ĩrĩa twathikĩrĩria andũ kĩũmbe makĩgayana maundũ mao ene, bamĩrĩ, na ng’ano cia ikundi, nĩtweĩgĩrĩire na ũmenyo wa bata wa marĩa mahĩtũku na wa andũ amwe arĩa maahutirie na njĩra njega kana njũru mũtugo wa gĩkundi gĩkĩ.
text_en: While listening to individuals share their individual, family, and organizational stories, we gained valuable insight into the past and some of the personalities who influenced for good or ill the culture of the organization.

text: O na harĩa mũndũ gũtaũkĩrwo nĩ rũgano rwake rwa marĩa mahĩtũku gũtiĩgeragĩria atĩ nĩũtaũkĩirwo nĩ mũtugo, nĩgũteithagia andũ o na arĩ o hanini magĩe na meeciria ma harĩa marĩ rũgano-inĩ rwa marĩa mahĩtũku ma gĩkundi.
text_en: While understanding one’s history does not assume understanding of culture, it does at least help people gain a sense of where they fall within the history of the organization.

text: Hĩndĩ ĩrĩa ũkũrora moohotani na ũkamenya maremwo, andũ kĩũmbe na arĩa othe maranyitanĩra kũmenya na njĩra ndiku makĩria maũndũ ma bata, wĩra, na maahinya marĩa matwarithagia gĩkundi.
text_en: While assessing the successes and becoming aware of failures, individuals and the whole of the participating persons discover more deeply the values, mission, and driving forces of the organization.

text: Ũndũ-inĩ ũyũ, kũririkana maũndũ mahĩtũku ma mũtugo wa wonjoria na moohotani marĩa maumanaga naguo nĩmateithirie andũ kũhĩmbĩria mogarũrũku meerũ na mwerekera mwerũ wa kanitha ya kwao.
text_en: In this instance, recalling previous instances of entrepreneurial behavior and resulting successes helped people to be open to new changes and new direction for the local church.

text: Ng’ano ta icio cia moohotani nĩcianyihanyihirie guoya wa ũgarũrũku na hĩndĩ o ĩo ũgathondeka mĩerekera mĩagĩrĩru kwerekera ũgarũrũku matukũ-inĩ marĩa marooka.
text_en: Such success stories lessened the fears of change, while creating positive inclinations toward change in the future.

text: Mwĩcirĩrie mwega nĩ urĩa urongoreirio guetha kĩhonia kia kũrehe mĩciirĩrie ĩtiganĩte hamwe nĩgũo gwetha kĩhonia.
text_en: Convergent thinking patterns are problem solving techniques that unite different ideas or fields to find a solution.

text: ũndũ ũrĩa waarĩ na bata mwĩcirĩrie inĩ wari ihenya, ũũgĩ na kwaga kuhĩtia, hamwe na kumenya ma, kũhũthĩra njĩra ĩria ciothe ciiho hamwe na kũmaatha moohoro.
text_en: The focus of this mindset is speed, logic and accuracy, also identification of facts, reapplying existing techniques, gathering information.

text: ũndũ ũrĩa wa bata mũno mwĩcirĩrie-ini ũyũ: Gũkoragwo na kĩhonia kĩmwe: Wĩchirie ũhoro wa ihonia igĩrĩ, wega kana ũru.
text_en: The most important factor of this mindset is: there is only one correct answer. You only think of two answers, namely right or wrong.

text: Mwĩcirĩrie wa mũthemba ũyũ ukuruhanĩte na maũndũ magainie na gĩthomo kĩa sayansi haamwe na miĩkie mĩtĩkĩrĩku ya maũndũ.
text_en: This type of thinking is associated with certain science or standard procedures.

text: Andũ arĩa makoragwo na mwĩcirĩrie ta ũcio nĩmahotaga kũririkana mĩtaratara, kũona ihonia na kũruta wĩra kũringana na ithimi cia sayansi.
text_en: People with this type of thinking have logical thinking, are able to memorize patterns, solve problems and work on scientific tests.

text: Andũ makoragwo handũ-inĩ ha gĩtĩĩna kĩnene marĩ ciũmbe iria irĩ iheeo harĩ gũthoma meeciria ma andũ arĩa angĩ.
text_en: Humans are by far the most talented species in reading the minds of others.

text: Ũũ nĩ kuuga nĩtũhotaga kwĩgereria tũtekũhĩtia ũrĩa andũ angĩ moyaga maũndũ, meendaga, metĩkagia, makamenya kana makerirĩria.
text_en: That means we are able to successfully predict what other humans perceive, intend, believe, know or desire.

text: Harĩ moohoti maya, gũtaũkĩrwo muoroto wa andũ arĩa angĩ nĩ wa bata. Ũtwĩtĩkagĩria gwetha kĩhonia kĩa maũndũ mangĩkorwo matiramenyeka wega ma ciĩko irooneka.
text_en: Among these abilities, understanding the intention of others is crucial. It allows us to resolve possible ambiguities of physical actions.

text: Ta kĩonereria, ũngĩona mũndũ agĩtua ndirica ya ngaari, kwahoteka wĩgererie atĩ ekũgeragia kũiya ngaari ya mũndũ ũtoĩo.
text_en: For example, if you were to see someone breaking a car window, you would probably assume he was trying to steal a stranger’s car.

text: No abatare gũtuĩrwo na njĩra ngũũrani angĩkorwo nĩegũteete cabi cia ngaari yake na atĩ nĩ ngaari yake mwene akũgeragia gũtua.
text_en: He would need to be judged differently if he had lost his car keys and it was his own car that he was trying to break into.

text: MRI yuumanĩte na magegania ma bĩthĩki meetagwo mũinaino wa magineti ya nuclear (NMR), ĩrĩa yahumbũrirwo mĩaka-inĩ ya ngiri ĩmwe na magana keenda ma mĩrongo ĩtatũ nĩ Felix Bloch (akĩruta wĩra thiinĩ wa cukuru ya mathomo ma igũrũ ya Stanford).
text_en: MRI is based on a physics phenomenon called nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), which was discovered in the 1930s by Felix Bloch (working at Stanford University) and Edward Purcell (from Harvard University).

text: thĩ-inĩ wa mũinaino ũyũ, nguucanio cia magineti na mĩrũri ya rĩdiũ ĩtũmaga atomu irekererie tũmenyithia tũnini twa rĩdiũ.
text_en: In this resonance, magnetic field and radio waves cause atoms to give off tiny radio signals.

text: Mwaka-inĩ wa ngiri ĩmwe na magana keenda ma mĩrongo mũgwanja , Raymond Damadian, ndagĩtari wa ũrigiti na mũthuthuria wa sayansi, akĩhumbũra kĩhumo gĩa kuoya mbica ũkĩhũthĩra mũinaino wa magineti ta kĩndũ gĩa gũthima mĩrimũ thĩ-inĩ wa ũrigiti.
text_en: In the year 1970, Raymond Damadian, a medical doctor and research scientist, discovered the basis for using magnetic resonance imaging as a tool for medical diagnosis.

text: Mĩaka ĩna thuutha-inĩ marũa ma kĩhooto kĩa mũthundũri nĩmaheanirwo, na nĩmo marĩ marũa ma mbere kũheanwo thĩ-inĩ wa thĩ ma kĩhooto kĩa mũthundũri mwena-inĩ wa MRI.
text_en: Four years later a patent was granted, which was the world's first patent issued in the field of MRI.

text: Mwaka-inĩ wa ngiri ĩmwe ya magana keenda ma mĩrongo mũgwanja na mũgwanja, Dr. Damadian akĩrĩkia mwako wa kĩmũrĩki kĩa MRI kĩa mbere kĩa “mwĩrĩ-wothe”, kĩrĩa etire kĩrĩa “Gĩtahootekaga”.
text_en: In 1977, Dr. Damadian completed the construction of the first “whole-body” MRI scanner, which he called the ”Indomitable”.

text: Kwaranĩria ũgĩtithagia nĩgũteithagĩrĩria gũthondeka ihinda rĩa gwĩcokera na gũcokeria arĩa angĩ.
text_en: Asynchronous communication encourages time for reflection and reaction to others.

text: Nĩ kũheaga arutwo ũhoti wa kuruta wĩra na mũthiĩre wao na kwerekeria mũthiĩre wa kũneanwo kwa ũhoro ũrutani-inĩ.
text_en: It allows students the ability to work at their own pace and control the pace of instructional information.

text: Hamwe na ũguo, gũkoragwo na mĩhaka mĩnini ya mahinda harĩ na ũhotekeku wa kũruta wĩra mathaa marĩa ũkwenda. (Bremer, 1998)
text_en: In addition, there are fewer time restrictions with the possibility of flexible working hours. (Bremer, 1998)

text: Ũhũthĩri wa nenda na rũrenda gwĩtĩkagĩria athomi makinyĩre uhoro mahinda mothe.
text_en: The use of the Internet and the World Wide Web allows learners to have access to information at all times.

text: Ningĩ arutwo no mahote kũneana ciũria kũrĩ arutani hĩndĩ o yothe na meerĩgĩrĩre macokio ma narua na kĩhooto, handũ ha gweterera nginya mũcemanio ũcio ũngĩ wa maitho kwa maitho.
text_en: Students can also submit questions to instructors at any time of day and expect reasonably quick responses, rather than waiting until the next face-to-face meeting.

text: Njĩra ya gũkĩrũka ũndũire wa kĩ-rĩu ũhoro-inĩ wa gũthoma nĩ ĩraheana wĩyathi kuuma kũrĩ mĩrũgamo ĩrĩa yoonekaga ta gũtarĩ na ĩngĩ ta yo. Gũtirĩ na njĩra ĩmwe njega ya gũthoma.
text_en: The postmodern approach to learning offers the freedom from absolutes. There is no one good way to learn.

text: Ũhoro wa ma, hatirĩ na ũndũ ũmwe mwega wa gũthoma. Gũthoma kũhaanĩkaga ũmenyeru-inĩ gatagatĩ ka mũthomi na ũũgĩ ũrĩa ũigĩtwo mbere yake.
text_en: In fact, there is not one good thing to learn.Learning takes place in the experience between the learner and the knowledge presented.

text: Ũmenyeru-inĩ witũ wa ihinda rĩrĩ kũrĩ na maingĩ megiĩ kwĩĩkĩra maũndũ na ũhoro ũraheanwo, cionanio cia TV ikuruhaine na gĩthomo nĩ ironania ũndũ ũyũ.
text_en: Our current experience with all the do-it-yourself and information presenting, learning-based television shows illustrates this point.

text: Aingĩ aitũ meekoraga makĩĩrorera moonanio ma TV marĩa matũmenyithagia mũtaratara kana ũmenyeru ũrĩa gũtarĩ hĩndĩ tũkanyitanĩra harĩ guo kana tũhũthĩre ũmenyi ũcio.
text_en: So many of us find ourselves watching a television show that informs us of a process or experience in which we will never participate or apply that knowledge.

text: Gũtirĩ hĩndĩ tũgathondeka ngaari, twake gĩthima rũgito rwa nyũmba iitũ, tũthiĩ thabarĩ ya Peru gũthũũrima mĩanangĩko ya tene, kana tũũmbe rĩngĩ nyũmba ya mũriganio witũ.
text_en: We will never overhaul a car, build a fountain in our backyard, travel to Peru to examine ancient ruins, or remodel our neighbour's house.

text: Thengiũ kũrĩ ũnyitithania wa ngucio cia rungu rwa iria cia baimba gũkinya Rũraya na mĩrũri ya satellite, Greenland nĩĩnyitithanĩtio wega na gĩcunjĩ kĩa mĩrongo kenda and ithatũ harĩ igana kĩa mũingĩ gĩgakinyĩra rũrenda rwa ũkinyanĩria.
text_en: Thanks to undersea fiber optic cable links to Europe and broadband satellite, Greenland is well connected with 93% of the population having internet access.

text: Mũkawa waku kana arĩa makũgwatĩte ũgeni (ũngĩkorwo ũgĩikara nyũmba ya ageni kana mũciĩ wa mũndũ kĩũmbe) harĩ na ũhotekeku wa gũkorwo na mĩrũri ya rũrenda rwa ũkinyanĩria kana PC ĩnyitithanĩtio na rũrenda rwa ũkinyanĩria, na ciikaro ciothe irĩ na nyũmba ya rũrenda rwa ũkinyanĩria kana handũ harĩ na mĩrũri ya rũrenda rwa ũkinyanĩria ya mũingĩ.
text_en: Your hotel or hosts (if staying in a guesthouse or private home) will likely have wifi or an internet connected PC, and all settlements have an internet cafe or some location with public wifi.

text: Ota ũria hekũgwetetwo hau kabere, ona korwo kiugo "Eskimo" nĩgĩtĩkĩrĩtwo bũrũrinĩ wa United States, nĩgĩkuagwo rĩnaihũthia kũrĩ andũ a Arctic arĩa matarĩ a bũrũri wa U.S, mũno mũno Canada.
text_en: As mentioned above, though the word "Eskimo" remains acceptable in the United States, it is considered pejorative by many non-U.S. Arctic peoples, especially in Canada.

text: Ona waigua kiugo kĩu gĩkĩhũthĩrwo nĩ aikari a Greenland, ũhũthĩrĩ wa kĩo niwagĩirwo gũithemwo nĩ oki.
text_en: While you may hear the word used by Greenlandic Natives, its use should be avoided by foreigners.

text: Aikari ambere a Greenland meĩtaga Inuit bũrũrinĩ wa Canada na Kalaalleq (uingĩ kalaallit) Greenlander thĩini wa Greenland.
text_en: The native inhabitants of Greenland call themselves Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, in Greenland.

text: Wĩki-naĩ, na muoroto mũũrũ kũrĩ ooki kwa njĩra o yothe, nĩ ũndũ ũtoĩkaine o na atĩa thĩ-inĩ wa Greenland. Nginya matũũra-inĩ, gũtirĩ “kũndũ kũũru.”
text_en: Crime, and ill-will toward foreigners in general, is virtually unknown in Greenland. Even in the towns, there are no "rough areas."

text: Rĩera ihehu kwahoteka no rĩo ũgwati wa kĩa biũ ũrĩa arĩa matehaarĩirie mangĩcemania naguo.
text_en: Cold weather is perhaps the only real danger the unprepared will face.

text: Ũngĩceerera Greenland hĩndĩ ya imera cia heho (ũkĩririkana atĩ o ũrĩa arathiĩ kwerekera rũgongo, noguo gũkũheha), nĩ ũndũ wa bata gũũka na nguo njiganu irĩ na ũrugarĩ.
text_en: If you visit Greenland during cold seasons (considering that the further north you go, the colder it will be), it is essential to bring warm enough clothing.

text: Mĩthenya ĩrĩa mĩraya mũno hĩndĩ ya ũrugarĩ no yerekerie mathĩĩna-inĩ ma kwaga toro mũiganu na mathĩĩna mangĩ makuruhaine ma ũgima wa mwĩrĩ.
text_en: The very long days in the summer can lead to problems getting sufficient sleep and associated health issues.

text: Hĩndĩ ya ũrugarĩ, ningĩ wĩhũge rwagĩ rwa Nordic. O na harĩa rũtatambagia mĩrimũ o yothe, no rũtuĩke rwa kũrakaria.
text_en: During the summer, also watch out for the Nordic mosquitoes. Although they do not transmit any diseases, they can be irritating.

text: O na harĩa mũtabarĩre wa kĩ-mbeca wa San Fracisco ũnyitanĩtio nĩ gũkorwo rĩrĩ kĩguucirĩrio kĩa agendi gĩa gĩkĩro gĩa kĩ-mabũrũri, mũtabarĩre warĩo wa kĩ-mbeca nĩ ũtiganĩte.
text_en: While San Francisco's economy is linked to it being a world-class tourist attraction, its economy is diversified.

text: Icigo iria nene cia waandĩkani nĩ mootungata moohĩgĩru, thirikari, mbeca, biacara, na ũgendi.
text_en: The largest employment sectors are professional services, government, finance, trade, and tourism.

text: Kuonanio kwa mahinda kwa mahinda kwa nyĩmbo, thenema, mabuku na ũndũire ũĩkaine nĩgũteithĩtie gũtũma itũũra rĩrĩ hamwe na itooka ciarĩo ituike cia kũmenyekana thĩ guothe.
text_en: Its frequent portrayal in music, films, literature and popular culture has helped make the city and its landmarks known throughout the world.

text: San Francisco nĩĩkũrĩtie mwako mũnene wa ũgendi ũrĩ na mĩkawa mĩingĩ mũno, mĩkawa ya irio, na nyũmba cia mĩcemanio cia gĩkĩro kĩa igũru.
text_en: San Francisco has developed a large tourist infrastructure with numerous hotels, restaurants, and top-notch convention facilities.

text: San Franscisco nĩngĩ nĩ kũndũ kũmwe gwa kũrĩa kwega mũno bũrũri-inĩ nĩ ũndũ wa mĩrugĩre ĩngĩ ya Asia: Korean, Thai, Indian, na Japanese.
text_en: San Francisco is also one of the best places in the nation for other Asian cuisine: Korean, Thai, Indian, and Japanese.

text: Gũthiĩ thabarĩ ya Thĩ ya Walt Disney kũrehanagĩre ũgendi mũnene harĩ bamĩrĩ nyingĩ cia America.
text_en: Traveling to Walt Disney World represents a major pilgrimage for many American families.

text: Iceera “kaingĩ” rĩkuruhanagia kũũmbũka gũthiĩ Kĩhaaro-inĩ kĩa Ndege gĩa Kĩ-mabũrũri kĩa Orlando, gũthiĩ na mbaathi nginya mũkawa wĩ hakũhĩ na Disney, gũikara ta kiumia kĩmwe hatarĩ kuuma indo-inĩ cia Disney, na gũcooka mũciĩ.
text_en: The "typical" visit involves flying into Orlando International Airport, busing to an on-site Disney hotel, spending about a week without leaving Disney property, and returning home.

text: Kũrĩ na maũndũ mangĩhoteka matiganĩte matarĩ mũthia, no ũndũ ũyũ ũgũikara o ũrĩa andũ aingĩ meendaga kuuga rĩrĩa mekwaria ũhoro wa “gũthiĩ Thĩ ya Disney”.
text_en: There are infinite variations possible, but this remains what most people mean when they talk of "going to Disney World".

text: Tigiti nyingĩ iria ciendagio nenda-inĩ kũhĩtũkĩra nenda ta eBay kana Craiglist nĩ tigiti hũthĩku gĩcunjĩ irĩ cia iceera rĩa mĩthenya mĩingĩ ihaaro-inĩ nyingĩ cia kũhuurũka.
text_en: Many tickets sold online through auction websites such as eBay or Craigslist are partially used multi-day park-hopper tickets.

text: O na harĩa ũndũ ũyũ wĩkĩkaga mũno, nĩũgirĩtio nĩ Disney: tigiti icio itingĩtiganĩrwo.
text_en: While this is a very common activity, it is prohibited by Disney: the tickets are non-transferable.

text: Camping oyothe rungu wa rim ya Grand Canyon nĩĩrabatara marũa ma backcountry.
text_en: Any camping below the rim in Grand Canyon requires a backcountry permit.

text: Marua cinyihagĩo kũgitĩra Canyon na cionekaga kuma mũthenya wa 1 wa mweri, mĩeri ĩna mbere ya mweri wa kwanjia.
text_en: Permits are limited to protect the canyon, and become available on the 1st day of the month, four months prior to the start month.

text: Nĩkĩo marũa ma backcountry mweri-inĩ wa gatano monekanaga mweri ĩmwe mweri-inĩ wa mũgaa.
text_en: Thus, a backcountry permit for any start date in May becomes available on 1 Jan.

text: Nabaathi cia matũra marĩa moĩkaine, ta Bright Angel Campground ĩrĩa ĩ hakanĩtie na Phantom Ranch, ihũragio nĩ mahoya ma mũthenya wa mbere kũhingũrwo.
text_en: Space for the most popular areas, such as the Bright Angel Campground adjacent to Phantom Ranch, generally fill up by the requests received on first date they are opened to reservations.

text: Kwĩna marũa nini cĩa kũingĩra na magũrũ ĩrĩa ciheanagwo kũrĩ a mbere gũkinya.
text_en: There are a limited number permits reserved for walk-in requests available on a first come, first served basis.

text: Kũingĩra Afrika Ya Mũhuro na njĩra ya ngaari nĩ njĩra ya magegania ya kuona ũthaka wothe wa gĩcigo kĩu o hamwe na gũkinya kũndũ kũrĩ nja ya njĩra iria ikoragwo kuo cia agendi.
text_en: Entering Southern Africa by car is an amazing way to see all the region's beauty as well as to get to places off the normal tourist routes.

text: Ũndũ ũyũ no wĩkwo ngaari-inĩ o yothe ĩkoragwo kuo harĩ na mũbango mũbacĩrĩre no ngaari ya 4x4 nĩĩrendekithio mũno na kũndũ kũingĩ no gũkinyĩrĩkire na ngaari yaambatĩrĩtio na thĩ nĩ magũrũ ya 4x4.
text_en: This can be done in a normal car with careful planning but a 4x4 is highly advised and many locations are only accessible with a high wheel base 4x4.

text: Iga meciria-inĩ hĩndĩ ĩrĩa ũkũbanga atĩ o na harĩa Afrika ya Mũhuro ĩrĩ nũmu wega ti mabũrũri mothe marigainie mahaana ta ũguo.
text_en: Keep in mind while planning that although Southern Africa is stable not all neighboring countries are.

text: Kũbatarĩka kwa marũa ma ũthaami na mathogora nĩgũtiganĩte kuuma bũrũri nginya bũrũri na maũndũ maya makinyanagĩrio nĩ bũrũri ũrĩa uumĩte.
text_en: Visa requirements and costs vary from nation to nation and are affected by the country you come from.

text: O bũrũri ningĩ nĩ ũrĩ na mawatho ma mwanya makĩonania nĩ indo irĩkũ cia hĩndĩ ya ũgwati ikũbatarĩka gũkorwo ngaari-inĩ.
text_en: Each country also has unique laws requiring what emergency items need to be in the car.

text: Victoria Falls nĩ itũũra rĩrĩ gĩcigo-inĩ kĩa mwena wa ithũĩro rĩa Zimbambwe, gũtuĩkanĩria mũhaka wa kuuma Livingstone, Zambia, na hakuhĩ na Botswana.
text_en: Victoria Falls is a town in the western portion of Zimbabwe, across the border from Livingstone, Zambia, and near Botswana.

text: Itũũra rĩrĩ rĩkoragwo o hakuhĩ na irurumo, na nĩcio kĩgucĩrĩrio kĩnene, no handũ haha harĩa hoĩkaine nĩ agendi nĩhaheanaga mĩeke mĩingĩ ya gũikaranga kũrĩ agendi a gwetha ikeno na agendi a kwĩrorera kũndũ na kũndũ.
text_en: The town lies immediately next to the falls, and they are the major attraction, but this popular tourist destination offers both adventure seekers and sightseers plenty of opportunities for a longer stay.

text: Kĩmera-inĩ kĩa mbura (Mweri wa Ikũmi na Ũmwe nginya Wa Gatatũ), mũigana wa maaĩ ũgakorwo ũrĩ igũrũ makĩria na Irurumo igakorwo irĩ na magegania makĩria.
text_en: In the rainy season (November to March), the water volume will be higher and the Falls will be more dramatic.

text: Ũrĩ na ũũma wa atĩ nĩũkũheha ũngĩkĩrĩra ndaraca-inĩ kana ũthiĩ na magũrũ rũterere-inĩ rwa tucĩra tũrĩa tũthiũrũrũkĩte hakuhĩ na Irurumo.
text_en: You are guaranteed to get wet if you cross the bridge or walk along the trails winding near the Falls.

text: Mwena ũrĩa ũngĩ, mũno nĩ tondũ wa mũigana wa maaĩ gũkorwo ũrĩ igũrũ mũno nĩkĩo kwĩrorera Irurumo cio nyene nĩgũgũthiĩkwo¬-nĩ maaĩ macio moothe!
text_en: On the other hand, it is precisely because the volume of water is so high that your viewing of the actual Falls will be obscured—by all the water!

text: Mbĩrĩra ya Tutankhamun (KV62). KV62 kwahoteka nĩyo ĩrĩ ngumo mũno harĩ mbĩrĩra ciothe iria irĩ Gituamba-inĩ, harĩa haarĩ na ũhumbũri wa Howard Carter wa ngiri ĩmwe ya magana keenda ma mĩrongo ĩĩrĩ na igĩrĩ wa handũ haarĩ o ta hagima ha gũthika athamaki harĩa mũthamaki mwĩthĩ aathikĩtwo.
text_en: Tomb of Tutankhamun (KV62). KV62 may be the most famous of the tombs in the Valley, the scene of Howard Carter's 1922 discovery of the almost intact royal burial of the young king.

text: Ĩkĩringithanio na mbĩrĩra nyingĩ cia gĩ-ũthamaki, o na kũrĩ ũguo, mbĩrĩra ya Tutankhamun ti ta ĩrĩ bata wa gũceererwo, ĩkĩrĩ nini makĩria na ĩrĩ na magemio o manini.
text_en: Compared to most of the other royal tombs, however, the tomb of Tutankhamun is barely worth visiting, being much smaller and with limited decoration.

text: Mũndũ o wothe ũrerirĩria kuona ũira wa kwanangwo gwa kĩguugua kĩu kũrĩa gwekirwo hĩndĩ ya kũgeria gũkĩruta kuuma ithandũkũ-inĩ nĩmegũkua ngoro tondũ no kĩongo na ciande cirooneka.
text_en: Anyone interested in seeing evidence of the damage to the mummy done during attempts to remove it from the coffin will be disappointed as only the head and shoulders are visible.
